Universals and variations in moral decisions made in 42 countries by 70,000 participants

We analysed responses to three sacrificial dilemmas collected from 70,000 participants in 42 countries in 2017 and 2018.

Results. Across countries, sacrificing one person to save five was considered acceptable in the Switch dilemma by 81% of participants on average, in the Loop dilemma by 72%, and in the Footbridge dilemma by 51%.

Published 2020.
